back: The death benefit stated in the policy, paid to the beneficiary upon the insured's death.
Used to calculate the premium: $$\frac{\text{Face Amount}}{1{,}000} \times \text{Rate per } \$1{,}000$$
Not necessarily the amount received if loans exist against the policy.
cards.front: Define [[kw:face amount]] in life insurance.

back: Temporary coverage for a specified period (1, 5, 10, 20 years).
Cheapest form; no cash value accumulates.
If the insured outlives the term, the policy expires with no value.
cards.front: What is [[kw:term insurance]]?
Explain [[kw:straight life (ordinary life) insurance]].
back: Permanent protection for the insured's entire life.
Higher premiums than term because a portion builds [[kw:cash value]].
The premium remains level for life.
Permanent coverage with premiums paid for only 20 years.
After 20 years, the policy is [[kw:paid‑up]]—no more premiums are due.
Cash value builds faster than straight life.
cards.front: What is [[kw:20‑payment life insurance]]?
List the three [[kw:nonforfeiture options]].
back: 1. Cash surrender – receive cash value; policy ends.
2. Reduced paid‑up insurance – use cash value to buy a smaller permanent policy with no further premiums.
3. Extended term insurance – use cash value to buy term insurance for the full face amount for a limited time.

cards.front: Cash value is $8,000. The rate for paid‑up insurance is $200 per $1,000. How much reduced paid‑up insurance can be purchased?
back: She would have $40,000 of paid‑up permanent insurance.

cards.front: How is the annual [[kw:fire insurance premium]] calculated?
back: $$\text{Annual Premium} = \frac{\text{Face Amount}}{100} \times \text{Rate per } \$100$$
Rates depend on construction type (frame, brick), occupancy, and fire protection.
Separate policies may be needed for building and contents.
Requires the insured to carry coverage equal to at least a specified percentage (usually 80%) of the property's value.
If underinsured, recovery for a partial loss is reduced: $$\frac{\text{Carried}}{\text{Required}} \times \text{Loss}$$
Encourages insuring to full value.
cards.front: What is a [[kw:coinsurance clause]] in fire insurance?
Compute coinsurance payment: value $300,000, insured for $200,000, 80% clause, loss $90,000.
What is the difference between [[kw:short‑rate]] and [[kw:pro‑rata]] cancellation refunds?
back: Short‑rate: if the insured cancels; uses a penalty table; refund is less.
Pro‑rata: if the insurer cancels; refund = Annual premium × (Remaining months / 12).
[[imp:Short‑rate always gives less refund than pro‑rata.]]
$$\text{ACV} = \text{Replacement Cost} - \text{Depreciation}$$
Standard fire policies pay ACV unless replacement cost coverage is added.
ACV leaves a gap that replacement cost coverage can fill.
cards.front: Define [[kw:actual cash value (ACV)]].
What are the three main types of auto insurance coverage?
back: [[kw:Liability]] – covers damage/injuries you cause to others (required).
[[kw:Collision]] – covers damage to your own car from a crash.
[[kw:Comprehensive]] – covers non‑crash damage (theft, fire, hail, animal strikes).
First number: max bodily injury per person ($100,000).
Second: max total bodily injury per accident ($300,000).
Third: max property damage per accident ($50,000).
If damages exceed limits, the insured pays the excess.
cards.front: Explain [[kw:split liability limits]] (e.g., 100/300/50).
What is a [[kw:deductible]] in auto insurance?
back: The amount the insured pays out‑of‑pocket before the insurer pays.
Applies to collision and comprehensive claims.
Higher deductible → lower premium, but more cost if a claim occurs.

cards.front: How is the insurer payment calculated with a deductible?
back: $$\text{Insurer Pays} = \text{Loss} - \text{Deductible}$$
If loss ≤ deductible, insurer pays $0.
For a total loss, insurer pays ACV minus deductible.
Insured pays the first $500.
cards.front: Collision damage $4,500, deductible $500. How much does the insurer pay?
List factors that affect [[kw:auto insurance premiums]].
back: Age, gender, driving record, location, vehicle type, coverage limits, deductibles.
Higher risk = higher premium.
Clean driving record and higher deductibles can lower premiums.
The insurer's right to recover the amount it paid from the at‑fault party's insurer.
If you're not at fault, your insurer may pay your claim and then seek reimbursement.
You may still need to pay your deductible upfront.
cards.front: What is [[kw:subrogation]]?
Your car (ACV $10,000) is totaled in a collision. Deductible $1,000. How much does your insurer pay?
back: Insurer pays ACV – deductible = $10,000 – $1,000 = $9,000.
You receive $9,000.
